text:
Work in the current directory using shell commands.
1. Write a file server.py: a Python 3 standard-library HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1:46205 that answers any GET with status 200 and the body "smoke ok".
2. Start it in the background and wait until it accepts connections.
3. Run exactly this and note what it prints:
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:46205/
4. Stop the server.
Then reply with one short sentence stating the HTTP status code curl printed and whether the server worked.

Running: python3 server.py & SERVER_PID=$!
for i in $(seq 1…

content.text:
{"command":"python3 server.py & SERVER_PID=$!
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  if curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 1 http://127.0.0.1:46205/; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2
done
echo "PID=$SERVER_PID"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:46205/
echo
kill $SERVER_PID
wait $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null
echo "server stopped""}
